candidates.phrase: immutable, immense, eternal, incomprehensible, almighty, most wise, most holy, most free
candidates.rationale: Directly predicates 'most wise' of the one true God as an essential divine attribute.
candidates.chunk_text: There is but one only, living, and true God, who is infinite in being and perfection, a most pure spirit, invisible, without body, parts, or passions; immutable, immense, eternal, incomprehensible, almighty, most wise, most holy, most free, most absolute; working all things according to the counsel of his own immutable and most righteous will, for his own glory; most loving, gracious, merciful, long-suffering, abundant in goodness and truth, forgiving iniquity, transgression, and sin; the rewarder of them that diligently seek him; and withal, most just, and terrible in his judgments, hating all sin, and who will by no means clear the guilty.

candidates.phrase: by his most wise and holy providence, according to his infallible foreknowledge
candidates.rationale: Asserts God governs all things by his own most wise providence, predicating wisdom of God himself.
candidates.chunk_text: God the great Creator of all things doth uphold, direct, dispose, and govern all creatures, actions, and things, from the greatest even to the least, by his most wise and holy providence, according to his infallible foreknowledge, and the free and immutable counsel of his own will, to the praise of the glory of his wisdom, power, justice, goodness, and mercy.

candidates.phrase: by the most wise and holy counsel of his own will, freely
candidates.rationale: Attributes God's eternal decree to his own most wise counsel, affirming divine wisdom.
candidates.chunk_text: God, from all eternity, did, by the most wise and holy counsel of his own will, freely, and unchangeably ordain whatsoever comes to pass: yet so, as thereby neither is God the author of sin, nor is violence offered to the will of the creatures; nor is the liberty or contingency of second causes taken away, but rather established.

candidates.phrase: knowing all things, most wise, most holy, most just, most merciful
candidates.rationale: Directly predicates 'most wise' of God himself among his essential attributes.
candidates.chunk_text: What is God? A. God is a Spirit, in and of himself infinite in being, glory, blessedness, and perfection; all-sufficient, eternal, unchangeable, incomprehensible, everywhere present, almighty, knowing all things, most wise, most holy, most just, most merciful and gracious, longsuffering, and abundant in goodness and truth.

candidates.phrase: the most wise, righteous, and gracious God
candidates.rationale: Explicitly names God as 'most wise' in describing his ordering of temptation.
candidates.chunk_text: What do we pray for in the sixth petition? A. In the sixth petition (which is, And lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from evil ), acknowledging that the most wise, righteous, and gracious God, for divers holy and just ends, may so order things, that we may be assaulted, foiled, and for a time led captive by temptations; that Satan, the world, and the flesh, are ready powerfully to draw us aside, and ensnare us; and that we, even after the pardon of our sins, by reason of our corruption, weakness, and want of watchfulness, are not only subject to be tempted, and forward to expose ourselves unto temptations, but also of ourselves unable and unwilling to resist them, to recover out of them, and to improve them; and worthy to be left under the power of them; we pray, that God would so overrule the world and all in it, subdue the flesh, and restrain Satan, order all things, bestow and bless all means of grace, and quicken us to watchfulness in the use of them, that we and all his people may by his providence be kept from being tempted to sin; or, if tempted, that by his Spirit we may be powerfully supported and enabled to stand in the hour of temptation; or when fallen, raised again and recovered out of it, and have a sanctified use and improvement thereof: that our sanctification and salvation may be perfected, Satan trodden under our feet, and we fully freed from sin, temptation, and all evil, forever.

candidates.phrase: God's decrees are the wise, free, and holy acts
candidates.rationale: Attributes wisdom to God's own decreeing acts, a narrower but wholly within-floor assertion.
candidates.chunk_text: What are the decrees of God? A. God’s decrees are the wise, free, and holy acts of the counsel of his will, whereby, from all eternity, he hath, for his own glory, unchangeably foreordained whatsoever comes to pass in time, especially concerning angels and men.

candidates.phrase: The Son is the Word, the Wisdom, and the image of the Father
candidates.rationale: Identifies the Son, who is fully God, as Wisdom itself, affirming wisdom of a divine person within the floor.
candidates.chunk_text: In keeping with this truth and Word of God we believe in one God, who is one single essence, in whom there are three persons, really, truly, and eternally distinct according to their incommunicable properties— namely, Father, Son, and Holy Spirit. The Father is the cause, origin, and source of all things, visible as well as invisible. The Son is the Word, the Wisdom, and the image of the Father. The Holy Spirit is the eternal power and might, proceeding from the Father and the Son. Nevertheless, this distinction does not divide God into three, since Scripture teaches us that the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit each has a distinct subsistence distinguished by characteristics— yet in such a way that these three persons are only one God. It is evident then that the Father is not the Son and that the Son is not the Father, and that likewise the Holy Spirit is neither the Father nor the Son. Nevertheless, these persons, thus distinct, are neither divided nor fused or mixed together. For the Father did not take on flesh, nor did the Spirit, but only the Son. The Father was never without the Son, nor without the Holy Spirit, since all these are equal from eternity, in one and the same essence. There is neither a first nor a last, for all three are one in truth and power, in goodness and mercy.

survivors.locator: Chapter 2.1 — Of God, and of the Holy Trinity
survivors.phrase: immutable, immense, eternal, incomprehensible, almighty, most wise, most holy, most free
survivors.rationale: Directly predicates 'most wise' of the one true God as an essential divine attribute.
survivors.chunk_text: There is but one only, living, and true God, who is infinite in being and perfection, a most pure spirit, invisible, without body, parts, or passions; immutable, immense, eternal, incomprehensible, almighty, most wise, most holy, most free, most absolute; working all things according to the counsel of his own immutable and most righteous will, for his own glory; most loving, gracious, merciful, long-suffering, abundant in goodness and truth, forgiving iniquity, transgression, and sin; the rewarder of them that diligently seek him; and withal, most just, and terrible in his judgments, hating all sin, and who will by no means clear the guilty.

survivors.phrase: infinite, eternal, and unchangeable, in his being, wisdom, power, holiness, justice, goodness and truth
survivors.rationale: The catechism directly predicates wisdom as an essential, infinite attribute of God's own being.
survivors.chunk_text: What is God? A. God is a spirit, infinite, eternal, and unchangeable, in his being, wisdom, power, holiness, justice, goodness and truth.

survivors.phrase: knowing all things, most wise, most holy, most just, most merciful
survivors.rationale: Directly predicates 'most wise' of God himself among his essential attributes.
survivors.chunk_text: What is God? A. God is a Spirit, in and of himself infinite in being, glory, blessedness, and perfection; all-sufficient, eternal, unchangeable, incomprehensible, everywhere present, almighty, knowing all things, most wise, most holy, most just, most merciful and gracious, longsuffering, and abundant in goodness and truth.

survivors.phrase: knowing all things, most wise, most holy, most just
survivors.rationale: Catechism defines God himself as most wise among his essential attributes.
survivors.chunk_text: Q. 7. What is God? A. God is a Spirit, in and of himself infinite in being, 2 glory, blessedness, and perfection; all-sufficient, eternal, unchangeable, incomprehensible, everywhere present, almighty; knowing all things, most wise, most holy, most just, most merciful and gracious, long-suffering, and abundant in goodness and truth.

survivors.phrase: completely wise, just, and good, and the overflowing source of all good
survivors.rationale: Confession directly attributes complete wisdom to the one God as an essential attribute.
survivors.chunk_text: We all believe in our hearts and confess with our mouths that there is a single and simple spiritual being, whom we call God— eternal, incomprehensible, invisible, unchangeable, infinite, almighty; completely wise, just, and good, and the overflowing source of all good.

survivors.phrase: by his most wise and holy providence, according to his infallible foreknowledge
survivors.rationale: Asserts God governs all things by his own most wise providence, predicating wisdom of God himself.
survivors.chunk_text: God the great Creator of all things doth uphold, direct, dispose, and govern all creatures, actions, and things, from the greatest even to the least, by his most wise and holy providence, according to his infallible foreknowledge, and the free and immutable counsel of his own will, to the praise of the glory of his wisdom, power, justice, goodness, and mercy.

survivors.phrase: the most wise, righteous, and gracious God
survivors.rationale: Explicitly names God as 'most wise' in describing his ordering of temptation.
survivors.chunk_text: What do we pray for in the sixth petition? A. In the sixth petition (which is, And lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from evil ), acknowledging that the most wise, righteous, and gracious God, for divers holy and just ends, may so order things, that we may be assaulted, foiled, and for a time led captive by temptations; that Satan, the world, and the flesh, are ready powerfully to draw us aside, and ensnare us; and that we, even after the pardon of our sins, by reason of our corruption, weakness, and want of watchfulness, are not only subject to be tempted, and forward to expose ourselves unto temptations, but also of ourselves unable and unwilling to resist them, to recover out of them, and to improve them; and worthy to be left under the power of them; we pray, that God would so overrule the world and all in it, subdue the flesh, and restrain Satan, order all things, bestow and bless all means of grace, and quicken us to watchfulness in the use of them, that we and all his people may by his providence be kept from being tempted to sin; or, if tempted, that by his Spirit we may be powerfully supported and enabled to stand in the hour of temptation; or when fallen, raised again and recovered out of it, and have a sanctified use and improvement thereof: that our sanctification and salvation may be perfected, Satan trodden under our feet, and we fully freed from sin, temptation, and all evil, forever.
